Monetary transmission mechanism or monetary transmission is the mechanism by which decisions about monetary policy affect the economy as a whole and the dynamics of inflation in particular. It describes the process by which the signal of the central bank about maintaining or changing the interest rate and its future trajectory is gradually transmitted from individual segments of the financial market to the real sector of the economy and, ultimately, to inflation.
